land.text: Abeokuta, built by Egba refugees (with Owu people) from the Oyo collapse round Olumo Rock

predecessors.note: The pages do not name the Oyo Empire; the Egba refugees and Owu people are the page's wording.

land.text: 'The Egba lands were incorporated into the colony of Nigeria by the British' in 1914, Abeokuta the provincial capital

successors.note: The Egba United Government page ends the government in 1918 after the Adubi War ('absorbed into the British colonial administration').

capitals.name: Abeokuta
capitals.note: Infobox capital Abeokuta; founded around 1830 at Olumo Rock.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. A 44 km circle round Abeokuta is about 6,000 km2, chosen to match the infobox figure (a fit, not an independent check). The page gives no boundaries; the Egba United Government of 1893 is the same territory.

ledger.note: c. 1830: the Egba found Abeokuta. The Egba 'established the town of Abeokuta around 1830 at what was then a small farming village'; Sodeke was chosen as leader; the infobox gives '1830: 6,000 km2'.

1851: Dahomey is beaten at Abeokuta. 'The Egba defeated King Gezo and the Dahomey incursion in the 1851 Battle of Abeokuta'; the Egba page dates the Egba-Dahomey conflict 1843-1851 and a decisive battle under Sodeke in 1851; 'They again beat back the Dahomey military in 1864.'
1851: the Dahomey attack on Abeokuta is repulsed; no land changes hands.

1893: the Egba confederacy is formalized as the Egba United Government. 'later formalized into the Egba United Government in 1893'; an alliance with the British governor Sir Gilbert Carter 'formalized the Egba United Government based in Abeokuta' (Abeokuta page); recognised in 1898 (EUG page).
1914: the Egba lands pass to the British. 'The Egba lands were incorporated into the colony of Nigeria by the British', Abeokuta the provincial capital.

1914: Egbaland is incorporated into Nigeria. The Egba United Government page keeps the government to 1918: 'In 1918, the Egba United Government was eventually absorbed into the British colonial administration', after the Adubi War (taxation and indirect rule).

wars.name: Egba-Dahomey wars
wars.outcome: The Egba beat the Dahomey army at the Battle of Abeokuta in 1851 (the conflict 'spanned 1843 to 1851') and 'again beat back the Dahomey military in 1864'; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The Dahomey page names an 1864 Dahomean operation against Abeokuta (three guns on locally made carriages) and gives no 1851 battle.

certainty.note: Only the 6,000 km2 area (1830) is given; no boundary.

sources.title: Egba United Government
sources.note: Infobox (6,000 km2 in 1830, capital Abeokuta); formalized 1893, recognised 1898, Gbadebo 1892-1920, Dahomey wars 1843-1851, absorbed 1918 after the Adubi War.

sources.title: Abeokuta
sources.note: Founded around 1830; battles with Dahomey 1851 and 1864; the 1893 alliance with Governor Carter; incorporated into the colony of Nigeria in 1914; Adubi War 1918.

notes: The Egba United Government has no Cliopatria row. Two pages opened. The infobox area (6,000 km2) is for 1830; the circle was sized to it. Disagreement: the Abeokuta page puts the incorporation into Nigeria in 1914, the Egba United Government page ends the government in 1918 (the Adubi War); the dossier ends in 1914 (explicit land event) and lists the Adubi War in `wars` outside its span (one validator warning). The government dates 1893 (formalization) vs 1898 (recognition by McCallum) and the Alake's reign (1892-1918 in the infobox, 1892-1920 in the text) also disagree on the page. Not on any page opened: the Ijaye War (1860-62), the Egba treaty of 1893 as such, any Ibadan conflict. The Egba lands overlap the Lagos Colony's Ogun State circle (Abeokuta was independent: the Lagos dossier does not list it as a protectorate). Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): the Adubi War (1918, Abeokuta page) was removed from wars because it lies outside the dossier's 1830-1914 life; it stays in the 1914 dissolve note.
